44.results: The Linnarsson run reached a mapping score of 0.470, and 0.473 in a rerun. After rescaling, each class took roughly 0.05 to 0.23 of a spot, so fractions were **near-uniform**. Across 25,660 spots, the top calls were Neurons 5,353, Immune 4,555, Vascular 3,810, Astrocytes 3,732 and Oligos 3,205. Immune as the top call in about 18% of spots is not plausible for brain tissue. The midbrain run was dominated by neuronal classes. It called only 128 spots OPC-Oligo, 95 Astro-Epen, 79 Vascular and 21 Immune. A midbrain reference does not match coronal forebrain sections. The spatial input was already log-transformed before re-normalisation, as a scanpy warning flagged. No Tangram output file was saved, and no later analysis uses this work. Deconvolution moved to cell2location with a combined reference (§45, §46).

45.how: Cell2location needs a single-cell reference to define each cell type's expression profile. The Chhatbar 2026 immune atlas contains only immune cells. Used alone, it would force neuronal signal into immune states. It was therefore grafted onto a whole-brain background from the Linnarsson adolescent atlas. Linnarsson classes were capped at 2,000 cells each, and its own Immune class was removed. Twelve Chhatbar immune identities were added with a "MYE:" prefix and also capped at 2,000 cells. The source atlas was kept as a batch key, so the model can absorb differences between the two datasets. Genes were then filtered by detection thresholds to build the signature matrix. Chhatbar functional modules were deliberately not used as labels; the finer subclass identities were. No validation was run at this step.
45.results: The combined reference had 25,113 cells and 19,917 genes in 18 types: 6 brain classes and 12 immune states. Neurons, Astrocytes, Oligos, PeripheralGlia, Vascular and four immune states, including microglia, had 2,000 cells each. Ependymal cells had 1,826, and the rarest states were NK at 336 and Treg at 353. After gene filtering, the signature matrix had 13,070 genes. The executed notebook shows 11,844 of these shared with the Visium data. The notebook's interpretation text and a memory note say 15,428 shared genes, which conflicts with the printed output. There is a cross-dataset batch effect between the two atlases. The brain background is coarse, since neurons are not split into subtypes. Several immune states have fewer than 400 cells, which makes their signatures less reliable.

46.how: The input was all 25,660 spots and 11,844 genes, with the 18-type combined reference from §45. Cell2location is a Bayesian model that explains each spot's counts as a mix of reference cell-type profiles. It estimates how many cells of each type each spot holds. A reference model learned the 18 profiles, and a spatial model with section as batch mapped them onto spots. It assumed about 30 cells per spot and ran 5,000 epochs on CPU, below the 30,000 recommended on GPU. Conservative abundance estimates were normalised per spot into fractions. For each region and immune state, section-level mean fractions were compared between BRICHOS and PBS with Mann-Whitney tests. No multiple-testing correction or slide control was applied. Anatomical plausibility was the only check on the deconvolution.
46.results: Mean composition was Neurons 0.375, Astrocytes 0.172, Oligos 0.082 and microglia 0.030 per spot. Regional patterns matched anatomy: corpus callosum was oligodendrocyte-rich and ventricular area ependymal-rich. Total immune reached about 24% per spot, which is inflated. The eight adaptive and peripheral states sat at a flat 1.5 to 2% floor with no spatial structure, a sign of **signature bleed**. Microglia were lowest in WT in all 10 regions. In spot-level means, BRICHOS was below PBS in 9 of 10 regions, for example caudoputamen 0.0256 vs 0.0284. In the section-level test, microglia were lower in BRICHOS in 7 of 9 regions. Five of 108 region-state rows hit the smallest possible p of 0.0238, with no FDR correction. A correction dated 2026-10-07 found the BRICHOS-below-PBS microglia trend is explained by slide P24215, not treatment. Once slide was modelled, the region-matched difference went from −5.2% to +1.2% (p = 0.70).

47.how: The first run spread immune mass across 12 similar rare signatures. This second run pruned the reference to sharpen the myeloid estimates. It kept the 6 brain classes plus microglia, border-associated macrophages (CAM), monocyte-derived macrophages (MDM), cDC1 dendritic cells and granulocytes. Seven adaptive lymphoid states were dropped. A headless script reused the cached reference and ran cell2location with the same settings as run 1. Cell2location estimates each spot's mix of reference cell types from its counts. A day later, the saved estimates were renormalised after dropping further types, to see which estimates were stable. A type whose fraction stays put across these scenarios is separable; one that shifts is soaking up leftover signal. It ran on the remote peer on 2026-09-17. There was no formal validation.
47.results: All numbers come from a memory note, because no outputs or notebook for this run are in the repository. Total immune fell to 17.4% per spot. A uniform floor of about 3% from cDC1, MDM and granulocytes remained. CAM did not localise to border or ventricular niches, sitting flat at about 0.03 everywhere. After post-hoc renormalisation, total immune was 8.8% and the microglia-only fraction 5.2%. The microglia fraction barely moved across scenarios (4.5% to 5.2%). The diagnosis was that **only microglia are separable** at Visium resolution with this atlas. BRICHOS was below PBS for microglia in 9 of 10 regions, with WT lowest. The 5.2% estimate does not match the 10.1% from the dedicated microglia-only run (§48). A correction dated 2026-10-07 attributes the BRICHOS-below-PBS direction to a slide P24215 offset (§51).

48.how: Runs 1 and 2 showed that only microglia could be separated. This run collapsed the immune compartment into one microglia class, so signal cannot bleed into junk signatures. The reference was 6 Linnarsson brain classes plus microglia. Cell2location estimates each spot's cell-type mix from its counts using these reference profiles. It ran on all 25,660 spots with about 12 cells per spot assumed, 5,000 spatial epochs on CPU and an 11,264-gene signature set. Outputs were per-spot fractions and region by treatment composition tables. The script itself is not in the repository; its settings are known from a memory note and the stereoscope docstring. Output tables are dated 2026-09-19, and notebook 09b was repointed to this run on 2026-09-25. No validation was run in this step. An independent method, stereoscope, later cross-checked it (§52, §53).
48.results: The run gave 25,660 spots by 7 types. Mean composition was Neurons 0.461, Astrocytes 0.176, microglia 0.101, Oligos 0.091, Ependymal 0.061, Vascular 0.059 and PeripheralGlia 0.050. Regional microglia ranged from 0.060 in WT ventricular area to 0.116 in PBS caudoputamen. WT was lowest of the three groups in all 10 regions. In meninges, for example, WT was 0.078, BRICHOS 0.096 and PBS 0.106. About 10% microglia per spot is roughly double the "about 5% expected" noted in notebook 09e. It is also double the 5.2% microglia-only estimate from the pruned run (§47). The WT difference is not clean evidence of disease-driven microgliosis. Notebook 09b later found BRICHOS below PBS in all 9 testable regions, which was also traced to slide (§49). The single WT section sits on slide P24215, which runs **low in microglia for every treatment** (§51).

49.how: This run reviews the output tables of cell2location run 3. Cell2location is a deconvolution method: it estimates what share of each spot's RNA comes from each cell type, using a single-cell reference. Run 3 used six brain classes plus one microglia class. No new model was fitted here. For each section and each annotated region, the notebook took the mean microglia fraction over that region's spots. These section-level means are the replicates, so each region has at most 6 PBS and 3 BRICHOS values. BRICHOS and PBS were compared per region with a Mann–Whitney U test. This is a rank test that asks whether one group's values tend to be higher than the other's, without assuming a normal distribution. Regions with fewer than two sections per arm were dropped, which removed thalamus. The output is a bar chart of BRICHOS minus PBS per region. There was no control for Visium slide and no correction for testing nine regions. With 6 versus 3 sections, the smallest possible p value is about 0.024. So no single region could ever reach strong significance. The review therefore reads the direction across regions more than any single p value.
49.results: BRICHOS had a lower mean microglia fraction than PBS in all nine testable regions. The gaps were small, from about 0.3 to 0.9 percentage points of spot composition. Meninges fell from 0.1055 under PBS to 0.0966 under BRICHOS. Hippocampal formation dropped by 0.0085 and caudoputamen by 0.0082 (p = 0.095). Only the ventricular area reached p below 0.05 (−0.0069, p = 0.048), and that is uncorrected. The other regions had p values between 0.17 and 0.57. At the time, the uniform direction was read as BRICHOS partly normalising microgliosis toward wild-type levels. **This reading did not hold.** A correction dated 2026-10-07 traced the uniform deficit to Visium slide P24215, which carries two of the three BRICHOS sections. The region-matched, slide-adjusted analysis (§51) moved the effect to about +1 %. BRICHOS section P28052_401, the only BRICHOS section on the PBS slide, sits inside the PBS range. The notebook also has stale text: its caveats cell still describes the earlier run 1 (24 % immune cells, p floor 0.0238). Its header still says "completed 2026-09-16".

50.how: This run is a visual sanity check of the deconvolution from cell2location run 3. Deconvolution here means estimating each spot's share of RNA from each cell type, using a single-cell reference. The notebook loads a compact bundle with spot coordinates, the H&E image and the seven cell-type fractions per spot. It draws several map types. Scatterpie maps put a small pie chart on every spot, one per treatment group. A single-section zoom and "zoom-in QC" windows of ±6 spots sit around region centres where the expected mix is known. For example, corpus callosum should be oligodendrocyte-rich and the ventricular area ependymal-rich. Because neurons dominate almost everywhere, pies blur together. So a "dominant-type segregation map" was added. Each cell type is z-scored across spots, meaning its fraction is expressed in standard deviations from its own average. Each spot is then coloured by the type that is most above its own average. This shows relative enrichment, not absolute abundance. The check is visual only, with no statistic. Its logic is simple: if the model put cell types in anatomically wrong places, its fractions could not be trusted downstream.
50.results: The maps cover 25,660 spots from 10 sections: 15,107 PBS, 7,596 BRICHOS and 2,957 wild-type spots. In the most-enriched map, spot counts were Neurons 7,817, Astrocytes 4,340, Microglia 3,892, Oligos 3,200, PeripheralGlia 2,919, Vascular 2,216 and Ependymal 1,276. The anatomy came out as expected. Ependymal signal sat on the ventricles. Oligodendrocytes sat in white matter. Vascular and peripheral glia signal sat at the meningeal rim. The zoom windows targeted corpus callosum, ventricular area, supragranular cortex and caudoputamen, and the catalogue notes they were judged by eye from the figure. No number summarises how well each window matched. So the conclusion is that the deconvolution is anatomically sensible, based on visual inspection only. Two warnings apply. Pies show proportions, not cell counts. The z-scored map shows which type is relatively enriched, so it can exaggerate small abundance differences, as §51 later showed. Some notebook text and three myeloid pie figures are stale leftovers from run 1.

51.how: This run asks whether PBS sections truly have more microglia, or only look that way. The impression came from z-scored maps, where each spot is coloured by its most relatively enriched type. The input is cell2location run 3 microglia fractions per spot. Cell2location is a deconvolution method that estimates each spot's cell-type shares from a single-cell reference. First, microglia were plotted on one shared absolute colour scale. Then each section's mean microglia fraction was computed, and PBS (6) versus BRICHOS (3) compared with a Mann–Whitney rank test. Sections were cut at different brain levels, so region mix could bias whole-section means. To fix this, only seven regions with at least 20 spots in every section were kept. Each region got equal weight. A mixed model was then fitted on section × region means. A mixed model is a regression that includes a per-section random offset, so spots or regions from one section are not treated as independent. It was fitted with region alone, then with region plus slide. Adding slide tests whether the deficit belongs to slide P24215 rather than to treatment. Finally, P28052_401 was compared with the PBS sections on its own slide.
51.results: Whole-section means showed no clear abundance effect. PBS averaged 0.1055 and BRICHOS 0.1002, a 5.0 % difference with p = 0.38. Section means varied only about 1.3-fold, from 0.086 (wild type) to 0.112 (a PBS section). The share of spots labelled "most-enriched microglia" varied about 7-fold, from 4.0 % to 26.8 %. So the z-scored map had magnified small differences. Region matching gave the same picture. On the seven common regions, BRICHOS was 5.2 % lower than PBS (rank test p = 0.26). The mixed model with region gave −5.2 % (p = 0.071). **With slide added, the effect became +1.2 % (p = 0.70).** BRICHOS 401, on the PBS slide, was also 1.2 % above the PBS mean, inside the PBS range of 0.1025 to 0.1105. All three sections on slide P24215 were low in every region: BRICHOS 201 (0.0942), BRICHOS 301 (0.1006) and wild type (0.0864). The conclusion is that BRICHOS does not change microglia abundance, and the apparent −5 % is a slide offset. The slide term rests on one BRICHOS section and the wild type. The mixed models gave boundary convergence warnings.

52.how: This run repeats the microglia deconvolution with a second, independent method. The aim is to check that the cell2location result is not a quirk of one model. Stereoscope is another deconvolution method. It first learns an expression profile for each reference cell type, then explains each spot's counts as a mix of those profiles. It also fits an extra "noise" component that absorbs counts the cell types cannot explain. To make the comparison fair, it used the same reference as run 3: six brain classes plus microglia. It also used the same 11,264 signature genes. The reference model trained for 400 epochs and the spatial model for 2,000 epochs on CPU. An epoch is one full pass over the training data. A first launch was stopped early. A second run trained fully but crashed while extracting proportions, which was fixed and resumed on 2026-10-23. The noise fraction was saved separately, and fractions were renormalised over the real cell types. Training loss curves (ELBO, the quantity the model minimises) were saved. They were used to check convergence, meaning whether the model had stopped improving.
52.results: With the noise component removed, mean shares per spot were Neurons 0.323, Astrocytes 0.176 and Microglia 0.169. The rest were Oligos 0.144, PeripheralGlia 0.097, Vascular 0.067 and Ependymal 0.024. Stereoscope therefore gives more microglia than cell2location, which gave about 0.101. It also gives fewer neurons. Before renormalisation, the noise component averaged 0.314 of each spot. So almost a third of the signal was not assigned to any cell type. **The reference model had not converged.** Its loss fell from 14.87 million to 6,615 and was still dropping 40.6 % over the last 100 epochs. The spatial model had plateaued, with a change of only −0.01 %. An under-trained reference means the cell-type profiles are not fully learned. That may explain part of the gap to cell2location, including the higher microglia and the large noise term. A rerun with 2,000 reference epochs would need full retraining. It was not launched and is pending the user's decision. The absolute fractions are model shares, not cell counts.

53.how: This run compares the two deconvolution methods spot by spot and section by section. Deconvolution estimates each spot's cell-type shares from a single-cell reference. The inputs are cell2location run 3 and the stereoscope run, both on the same 25,660 spots and seven cell types. Three comparisons were made. First, for each cell type, the per-spot fractions from both methods were correlated. Pearson correlation measures linear agreement; Spearman (ρ) measures agreement in ranking. Second, mean microglia per section was computed under each method, grouped by slide. PBS and BRICHOS were compared with a Mann–Whitney rank test. This checks whether stereoscope also shows sections on slide P24215 as microglia-low. Third, microglia "hotspots" were defined in each method as spots with a microglia z-score above 1.5, meaning 1.5 standard deviations above the global average. Their overlap was measured with the Jaccard index: shared spots divided by spots flagged by either method. If both methods agree on where microglia are, the downstream hotspot analyses are not method artefacts. The comparison ran locally from saved tables on 2026-10-23.
53.results: Per-spot agreement for microglia was moderate. Pearson r was 0.541 and Spearman ρ 0.481, the weakest of the seven types. The other types reached r = 0.63 to 0.75. Mean microglia was 0.101 under cell2location and 0.169 under stereoscope. Hotspots overlapped partly. Cell2location flagged 1,644 spots, stereoscope 1,300, and 1,050 were shared, a Jaccard index of 0.55. Section means correlated between methods with Spearman 0.503. Neither method showed a significant PBS versus BRICHOS difference: stereoscope 0.1764 vs 0.1623 (p = 0.167), cell2location 0.1055 vs 0.1002 (p = 0.381). The slide pattern was only partly reproduced. Under stereoscope, P24215_301 (0.145) and wild type (0.144) were low, and BRICHOS 401 (0.176) sat inside the PBS range. **But on whole-section means, BRICHOS P24215_201 (0.166) sat inside the PBS range too.** On the seven common regions, however, 201 is low under stereoscope, at about 89 % of the PBS mean. So the slide pattern depends on whether region mix is controlled. Stereoscope's reference was under-converged (§52), and its noise term varies by region (§56).

54.how: Earlier notebooks found that BRICHOS shifts microglia toward a homeostatic (resting) state. That finding used cell2location microglia weights. This run checks whether it depends on the deconvolution method. Per-spot signature scores were taken from the inflammation analysis. They summarise expression of curated gene sets: homeostatic microglia genes, DAM genes, and the DAM:homeostatic ratio (DAM minus homeostatic). DAM means disease-associated microglia, the plaque-reactive state. Two tests were run with each method's microglia fractions. In test A, each section's mean score was weighted by microglia fraction, so microglia-rich spots count more. PBS (6) and BRICHOS (3) were compared with a Mann–Whitney rank test. In test B, only hotspot spots were used, meaning microglia z-score above 1.5. A mixed model then compared treatments. This is a regression with a random offset per section, so spots from one section are not counted as independent. Scores were z-scored, so effects are in standard-deviation units. The model was fitted without and with slide as a covariate. Adding slide asks whether the effect belongs to Visium slide P24215 rather than to BRICHOS.
54.results: The state shift appeared under both methods, so it is not a cell2location artefact. In weighted section means, the DAM:homeostatic ratio was lower under BRICHOS by 0.0258 (cell2location) and 0.0271 (stereoscope). Both had p = 0.0238, the smallest p possible with 6 versus 3 sections. Homeostatic rose by 0.0145 (p = 0.26) and 0.0326 (p = 0.095). DAM itself did not move clearly. In hotspot mixed models, the homeostatic score was 0.385 standard deviations higher under BRICHOS with cell2location (p = 0.026). It was 0.495 higher with stereoscope (p = 0.003). **With slide added, both effects shrank and lost significance**: 0.222 (p = 0.41) and 0.287 (p = 0.22). The DAM:homeostatic ratio went from −0.251 to −0.090 (cell2location) and from −0.262 to −0.088 (stereoscope), all non-significant. Slide-adjusted models gave convergence warnings, though the notebook says the estimates were stable across optimisers. The conclusion is that the state shift is method-independent but cannot be separated from slide.

55.how: This run repeats the region-matched microglia abundance test of §51 under both deconvolution methods. Deconvolution estimates each spot's cell-type shares from a single-cell reference; here cell2location and stereoscope were used. Brain sections were cut at different levels, so whole-section means mix different regions. To avoid this, only regions with at least 30 spots in all ten sections were kept. These were the same seven regions as in §51. For each region, BRICHOS was expressed as a percentage difference from the PBS mean. That was tested with a Mann–Whitney rank test on section means. Then a mixed model was fitted on section × region values, with the response scaled to percent of the PBS mean. A mixed model is a regression with a random offset per section. So one section's seven region values are not counted as independent evidence. The model included treatment and region, and then also slide. Comparing the two fits tells whether the BRICHOS deficit is really a property of slide P24215. Running both methods asks whether the answer depends on the deconvolution model.
55.results: Both methods showed lower microglia under BRICHOS in most regions before slide was modelled. The sign agreed in six of seven regions, and the region-level differences correlated with Spearman 0.536. Stereoscope gave larger gaps: for example caudoputamen −7.1 % (cell2location) vs −14.7 % (stereoscope), and supragranular −4.5 % vs −15.7 %. Meninges was −8.4 % (p = 0.167) and −9.9 % (p = 0.048). In the mixed model, cell2location gave −5.21 % (p = 0.071). Stereoscope gave −7.76 % (p = 0.034). **With slide in the model, both moved to about +1 %**: +1.23 % (p = 0.70) and +0.81 % (p = 0.88). So the apparent microglia reduction comes from slide P24215 under both methods. It is not a cell2location artefact, and it is not a treatment effect. The large stereoscope gaps in cortex and striatum are partly inflated by renormalising away its noise term (§56). On these seven regions, BRICHOS P24215_201 is low under stereoscope, at about 89 % of PBS. On whole-section means it sits inside the PBS range. Only 6 PBS and 3 BRICHOS sections are available.

56.how: Stereoscope, the second deconvolution method, fits an extra "noise" component. This absorbs counts that no reference cell type explains. After the model is fitted, the noise share is dropped and the remaining cell-type fractions are rescaled to sum to one. That rescaling is safe only if the noise share is similar across the groups being compared. If noise differed by slide or treatment, rescaling alone could create or hide a microglia difference. This run checks that. It took the per-spot noise share saved from the stereoscope run. It computed the mean noise share per section and compared the two Visium slides with a Mann–Whitney rank test. It also computed mean noise share per brain region. Finally, it correlated per-spot noise with each method's microglia fraction using Spearman correlation, which compares rankings rather than raw values. A link between noise and microglia would mean the renormalisation stretches microglia estimates where noise is high. There is no formal test of region effects; the regional means are descriptive.
56.results: Noise did not track slide or treatment. Section means ranged from 0.233 to 0.384. They split into a group near 0.24 (P28052_102, P28052_103 and P24215_201) and a group near 0.35 (the rest). By slide, P28052 averaged 0.328 and P24215 0.295, with p = 0.517. **Noise was strongly regional.** It was 0.037 in the ventricular area and 0.076 in hypothalamus. It reached 0.465 in caudoputamen and 0.549 in infragranular cortex. Per spot, noise correlated −0.521 with stereoscope microglia and +0.307 with cell2location microglia. So where noise is high, stereoscope assigns less microglia before rescaling, and the rescaling then stretches whatever difference remains. The regions with about 50 % noise, caudoputamen and infragranular cortex, are where stereoscope shows its largest BRICHOS versus PBS gaps. Those gaps should be read as amplified. The under-trained reference model (§52) may also inflate the noise term. The main conclusion is reassuring: noise does not create a slide or treatment artefact on its own.

57.how: This run reviews the stereoscope deconvolution in the same way §49 reviewed cell2location run 3. Deconvolution estimates each spot's cell-type shares from a single-cell reference. Stereoscope is the second, independent method. The unit is a section × region mean microglia fraction, using regions with at least 30 spots in a section. Regions also needed at least two sections per arm. For each region, the 3 BRICHOS sections were compared with the 6 PBS sections using a Mann–Whitney rank test. With 6 versus 3, the smallest possible p value is about 0.024. There was no correction for testing seven regions and no slide term in this test. To see which sections drive any difference, the notebook drew per-section dot plots by region, with slide shown as marker shape. This lets the reader check whether the P24215 BRICHOS sections and the P28052 BRICHOS section behave alike. If they differ, slide rather than treatment is the likely cause. The notebook also mapped the noise term by region and section and listed caveats. It was written and revised on 2026-10-23.
57.results: BRICHOS had lower microglia than PBS in five of seven regions. Caudoputamen fell from 0.1854 to 0.1582 (−14.7 %, p = 0.26). Supragranular cortex was −15.7 % (p = 0.26), olfactory areas −10.9 % and infragranular cortex −9.0 %. Only meninges reached p below 0.05: −9.9 %, p = 0.048, uncorrected. Hypothalamus (−0.6 %) and corpus callosum (+0.7 %) showed nothing. The dot plots show the shift is carried by BRICHOS 201 and 301 on slide P24215. BRICHOS 401, on the PBS slide, sits within the PBS range. On the seven common regions, 201 is low, at about 89 % of the PBS mean. On whole-section means, 201 sits inside the PBS range. **With slide in the model, the effect disappears**: −7.8 % becomes +0.8 % (§55). The notebook lists further caveats. The reference model was under-converged. The 0.17 level is not a cell count. Noise is regional and stretches cortex and striatum effects. Per-spot agreement with cell2location is only moderate. This review therefore does not support a BRICHOS effect on microglia abundance.

58.how: This run asks whether BRICHOS reduces neuroinflammation. If so, is it through fewer microglia, or through microglia in a calmer state? Full Visium counts for 25,660 spots were normalised and log-transformed. Five curated gene signatures were scored per spot. These were homeostatic microglia, DAM (disease-associated microglia, the plaque-reactive state), neuroinflammation, complement and reactive astrocytes. A DAM:homeostatic ratio was defined as DAM minus homeostatic. Microglia hotspots were spots whose deconvolution microglia fraction was 1.5 standard deviations above average, giving 1,644 spots. Deconvolution estimates each spot's cell-type shares from a single-cell reference. The main test was a mixed model on the 1,599 PBS and BRICHOS hotspot spots. That is a regression with a random offset per section, so spots in one section are not treated as independent. A sensitivity test compared section means with a Mann–Whitney rank test (6 vs 3). Hotspot counts were also summed per section and tested gene by gene with DESeq2. Genes were then ranked and tested with GSEA. GSEA asks whether a gene set sits near the top or bottom of a ranked list. Wild type (one section) was descriptive only.
58.results: Microglia abundance in hotspots did not differ: 0.151 under PBS and 0.152 under BRICHOS (p = 0.26). The homeostatic signature was higher under BRICHOS. The mixed model gave β = +0.077 (p = 0.013). Section means rose from 0.445 to 0.521, but that test gave only p = 0.095. The DAM:homeostatic ratio was lower as a trend (β = −0.040, p = 0.056). DAM, neuroinflammation, complement and reactive astrocyte scores did not change. In GSEA, the homeostatic set was enriched under BRICHOS (NES +2.06, q < 0.001), led by P2ry12, Cx3cr1, Hexb and Csf1r. The reactive astrocyte set was depleted (NES −1.81, q = 0.005). No single gene passed false discovery correction; the best was Ganab, adjusted p = 0.18. Untested regional means suggested the largest ratio drops in thalamus, olfactory areas and meninges. **Two later corrections weaken this result.** With slide as a covariate, the homeostatic effect fell to p = 0.30 and the ratio to p = 0.61 (§62). Within-section niche contrasts showed no treatment effect on any microglial state (§67). The finding is therefore slide-confounded and not confirmed.

59.how: This run checks the state shift from §58 against two simple alternative explanations. The first is the hotspot cutoff. The original analysis kept spots whose microglia fraction was more than 1.5 standard deviations above average. That cutoff is arbitrary, so the test was repeated at 1.0 and 2.0. The second alternative is abundance. If BRICHOS hotspots held slightly fewer microglia, their signature scores could differ for that reason alone. So each model was fitted without and with the spot's microglia fraction as a covariate. The data and scoring were the same as §58. Only three signatures were tested: homeostatic, DAM (disease-associated microglia) and the DAM:homeostatic ratio. The model was the same mixed model: score by treatment, with a random offset per section. That offset stops spots from one section being counted as independent replicates. The output is the BRICHOS minus PBS effect with its 95 % confidence interval and p value. This check does not include Visium slide, so it cannot address the slide confound.
59.results: Hotspot sizes changed with the cutoff. PBS and BRICHOS had 2,427 and 884 spots at z > 1.0. They had 1,123 and 476 at z > 1.5, and 550 and 249 at z > 2.0. The DAM:homeostatic ratio stayed lower under BRICHOS at every cutoff. After adjusting for microglia fraction, it was significant at all three. At z > 1.0, p moved from 4.5e-5 unadjusted to 2.9e-6 adjusted (β = −0.047). At z > 1.5, p moved from 0.056 to 0.022 (β = −0.044). At z > 2.0, p moved from 0.054 to 0.033 (β = −0.070). The homeostatic score was significant after adjustment at z > 1.0 (p = 0.0024) and z > 1.5 (p = 0.016). It was not significant at z > 2.0 (p = 0.090). DAM was never significant. So the shift is robust to the cutoff and to abundance. These are spot-level p values, and nine sections give a poorly estimated section variance. **A correction dated 2026-09-25 notes the result is not robust to slide** (§62).

60.how: This run removes the hotspot cutoff entirely. Instead of keeping only microglia-rich spots, it uses every spot but weights it by its microglia fraction. The fraction comes from cell2location deconvolution, which estimates each spot's cell-type shares from a single-cell reference. Microglia-rich spots then dominate the average smoothly. This brings the result closer to a "pure microglia" state measurement without an arbitrary threshold. Signatures were scored as in §58: homeostatic microglia, DAM (disease-associated microglia) and the DAM:homeostatic ratio. For each section, a weighted mean of each signature was taken, with negative weights clipped to zero. That gives one value per section. PBS (6 sections) and BRICHOS (3 sections) were compared with a Mann–Whitney rank test. With 6 versus 3, the smallest possible p value is about 0.024. Wild type was reported as a single descriptive value. This run has no slide term. Per-section values were also listed, so the reader can see which sections drive any difference.
60.results: The DAM:homeostatic ratio was lower under BRICHOS. PBS averaged 0.324 and BRICHOS 0.298, a difference of −0.026 with p = 0.024. That is the smallest p value possible with 6 versus 3 sections, so all three BRICHOS sections ranked below all six PBS sections. Wild type was 0.253. The homeostatic score rose by 0.015 (p = 0.26), and DAM fell by 0.011 (p = 0.38). Neither was significant. **The per-section values point to slide.** The two BRICHOS sections on slide P24215 had the lowest ratios among Alzheimer-model sections, 0.285 and 0.301. BRICHOS P28052_401, on the PBS slide, had 0.309. PBS sections ranged from 0.313 to 0.332, so 401 sits just below the PBS range. Slide P24215 also carries the wild-type section, which is lowest of all. So the lower ratio is driven mostly by the P24215 sections. This is the same slide confound later quantified in §62, where adding slide removes the significance.

61.how: The regional bars in §58 suggested the strongest calming in thalamus, olfactory areas and meninges. This run asks whether the BRICHOS state effect really differs between regions. The unit is hotspot spots, meaning spots whose microglia fraction is more than 1.5 standard deviations above average. Only regions with at least 20 PBS and 20 BRICHOS hotspot spots were kept. Eight regions qualified; thalamus dropped out for too few BRICHOS spots. Two analyses were run. First, a likelihood-ratio test compared two mixed models. A mixed model is a regression with a random offset per section. A likelihood-ratio test asks whether a more complex model fits clearly better. Here the complex model lets the treatment effect differ by region; the simple one forces a single effect. If the complex model does not fit better, there is no evidence for region-specific effects. Second, BRICHOS minus PBS differences were computed per region from section means and tested with a Mann–Whitney rank test. Power is low: 6 versus 3 sections gives a minimum p of about 0.024. The analysis has no slide term.
61.results: There was no significant treatment × region interaction. The likelihood-ratio p was 0.19 for the DAM:homeostatic ratio, 0.42 for homeostatic and 0.60 for DAM. These values come from the script printout recorded in notebook 11 and memory; they are not in a saved table. For the DAM:homeostatic ratio, six of eight regions moved downward under BRICHOS. None was significant. Meninges had the largest drop, −0.159 (p = 0.26). Olfactory areas followed at −0.134 (p = 0.17). Hippocampal formation was −0.057 but rests on only 2 PBS and 1 BRICHOS section. Corpus callosum (−0.041), infragranular (−0.034) and supragranular (−0.007) were small. Caudoputamen (+0.027) and hypothalamus (+0.029) went the other way. So the earlier impression of strongest calming in thalamus was descriptive only, and thalamus could not be tested here. **The data do not support a region-specific state effect.** The analysis is underpowered and not adjusted for slide, so a regional effect cannot be ruled out either.

62.how: A spatial map seemed to show fewer microglia under BRICHOS. Inspecting the sections by Visium slide revealed the confound. All six PBS sections are on slide P28052. Two of three BRICHOS sections and the wild type are on P24215. This run tests how much of the BRICHOS effect is slide. For abundance, the mean microglia z-score of each section was plotted and coloured by slide. Whole-section abundance was compared between PBS and BRICHOS at section level. For microglial state, the hotspot mixed model of §58 was refitted with slide as an extra fixed effect. A mixed model is a regression with a random offset per section. A fixed slide term absorbs any constant shift shared by all sections on one slide. After that, the only treatment contrast left is within slide P28052: six PBS sections versus one BRICHOS section, P28052_401. If the effect were truly treatment, it should survive this adjustment. No script for this step is in the repo. It was computed ad hoc, and only the figure and the table were committed.
62.results: Whole-section abundance did not differ clearly. PBS averaged 0.106 and BRICHOS 0.100 (p = 0.38). Hotspot burden was 7.5 % versus 6.3 % (p = 0.55), a value stated only in notebook text. Slide P24215 runs low in microglia whatever the treatment. Read off the figure, section z-scores were −0.72 for wild type, −0.44 for BRICHOS 201 and −0.05 for BRICHOS 301. BRICHOS 401, on P28052, sat inside the PBS range at +0.32. The PBS range was about −0.19 to +0.48. **Adding slide removed the significance of the state effects.** The homeostatic effect fell from β = 0.077 (p = 0.013) to 0.045 (p = 0.30). The DAM:homeostatic ratio fell from −0.040 (p = 0.056) to −0.013 (p = 0.61). DAM stayed non-significant (p = 0.63). The direction held, but the effects roughly halved. The homeostatic signal is therefore hypothesis-generating, not confirmatory. Slide and treatment cannot be separated, because the adjusted estimate rests on one section. Notebook 17 later showed a region-matched abundance version: −5 % becomes +1 % with slide (p = 0.70).

63.how: This run asks whether a model can recognise treatment in a section it has never seen. Validation was leave-one-section-out: train on all sections but one, then predict the held-out section. Random spot splits would leak, because spots from one section share identity. Each training section contributed 800 spots. A held-out section's score was its mean predicted probability of BRICHOS. Gene selection, scaling and principal components were refitted inside each fold on training sections only. The model was L2-regularised logistic regression, a linear classifier with a penalty that keeps weights small. Four feature sets were compared. QC features (counts, genes, mitochondrial and ribosomal share) are a technical negative control: they carry no biology. Others were 23 signature scores, 30 principal components, and 2,000 highly variable genes. The same pipeline also predicted slide, as a batch baseline. Two nulls were used. All 84 ways of relabelling 3 of 9 sections as BRICHOS gave a permutation p (floor 0.012). A slide-conditional test asked whether 401 ranks first among the seven P28052 sections. Treatment and slide gene weights were also correlated.
63.results: This run applied no confound removal. **The best treatment classifier was the QC-only model**, with AUC 1.00 and permutation p = 0.012. AUC is the chance that a random BRICHOS section scores above a random PBS section; 0.5 is guessing. QC features also predicted slide perfectly. Signature scores gave treatment AUC 0.61 (p = 0.32). Principal components gave 0.89 (p = 0.048), and highly variable genes 0.78 (p = 0.083). The same feature sets predicted slide with AUC 0.67, 0.90 and 0.95. BRICHOS 401 ranked first among P28052 sections for QC, signatures and PCA. In PCA it nearly tied with PBS section 301 (0.444 vs 0.434). In the gene model, PBS 301 ranked first. Treatment and slide models used the same genes, with weights correlated at r = 0.57. BRICHOS-ward genes included immediate-early genes (Egr1, Arc, Nr4a1, Klf2), hypothalamic neuropeptides (Avp, Oxt) and Hexb. PBS-ward genes included Pmch, Hcrt, Ttr, Pomc and Slc17a7. The QC signal is attributed to sequencing depth, lower on P24215. Those depth medians appear in memory and notebook 17 but not in any saved output.

64.how: The first classifier (§63) separated treatments mainly through sequencing depth. This run removes depth and asks whether any treatment signal remains. Every spot was binomially downsampled to exactly 5,000 UMI. A UMI is one counted RNA molecule. Downsampling randomly discards counts until every spot has the same total, so depth can no longer differ between sections. Spots with fewer than 5,000 UMI were dropped, leaving 24,653 of 25,660. Everything else was the same as §63. Validation was leave-one-section-out, with preprocessing refitted inside each fold. The model was penalised logistic regression. The four feature sets were QC metrics, signature scores, principal components and highly variable genes. Each was trained to predict treatment and, separately, slide. The permutation null relabelled every possible set of 3 BRICHOS among 9 sections. A slide-conditional rank asked where BRICHOS 401 falls among the seven P28052 sections. Per the run log, immediate-early genes were kept and regions were not matched. The QC set acts as a technical control. If depth was the driver, its treatment signal should vanish here.
64.results: Downsampling removed the QC-based treatment signal. The QC model's treatment AUC fell from 1.00 to 0.67 (p = 0.26), and 401 now ranked last (7/7) on its slide. AUC is the chance that a random BRICHOS section scores above a random PBS section; 0.5 is guessing. **But QC features still predicted slide** with AUC 0.95. Downsampling equalises total counts, but library complexity and ribosomal share still differ by slide. No expression model beat the permutation null. Signatures gave treatment AUC 0.61 (p = 0.27). Principal components gave 0.67 (p = 0.095), and highly variable genes 0.72 (p = 0.071). For PCA and genes, 401 ranked second on its slide, behind PBS section 301. Slide AUC stayed between 0.67 and 0.95. Treatment and slide models still used the same genes, with weights correlated at r = 0.64. BRICHOS-ward genes were still Egr1, Nr4a1, Arc, Oxt and Avp. PBS-ward genes now included immune genes: Cst3, Igkc, Cd74, C3 and Apoe. Depth is removable, but slide is not.

65.how: After depth was removed (§64), the top classifier genes were immediate-early genes and region markers. Immediate-early genes are fast-response genes like Egr1 and Arc, often switched on by tissue handling stress. Region markers can reflect where each section was cut. This run removes both. It uses the same leave-one-section-out classifier as §63 and §64. Spots were downsampled to 5,000 UMI so sequencing depth is equal. Thirty-six immediate-early and stress genes were dropped. Only the seven regions with at least 30 spots in every section were kept, leaving 21,867 spots. Each region got equal weight within a section, both in training and in the held-out section's score. This stops a section from looking different just because it contains more of one region. The four feature sets were QC metrics, signature scores, principal components and highly variable genes. The model was penalised logistic regression. Nulls were the 84-relabelling permutation test and the rank of 401 among P28052 sections. If treatment signal existed beyond these nuisances, it should now rise above the null.
65.results: No treatment signal rose above the permutation null. QC features gave treatment AUC 0.67 (p = 0.21). AUC is the chance that a random BRICHOS section scores above a random PBS section; 0.5 is guessing. Signature scores gave 0.50 (p = 0.30), no better than chance. Principal components gave 0.83 (p = 0.060), the closest to significance. Highly variable genes gave 0.67 (p = 0.11). **Slide stayed predictable**, with AUC from 0.71 to 1.00. BRICHOS 401 ranked sixth of seven on its slide for QC and signatures. It ranked second, behind PBS section 301, for PCA and genes. Treatment and slide models still used the same genes, correlated at r = 0.64. Top genes still included hypothalamic neuropeptides and transcription factors. Oxt, Sim1, Avp and Shox2 were BRICHOS-ward; Pmch, Hcrt and Prl were PBS-ward. So region matching did not remove differences in the sub-regional cutting plane. This run is not shown in notebook 17. That notebook's "depth-matched" row loads the §64 run but describes this run's settings.

66.how: Hypothalamic neuropeptides survived region matching in §65. That suggested differences in where sections were cut, known as the cutting plane. This run removes that anatomy as well. It keeps all earlier steps: downsampling to 5,000 UMI per spot, dropping 36 immediate-early genes, and matching seven shared regions with equal weights. It then also drops the hypothalamus region. It also drops 40 genes. These include hypothalamic neuropeptides and hormones such as Oxt, Avp, Pmch, Hcrt and Pomc. They also include hypothalamic transcription factors (Sim1, Otp, Shox2) and choroid plexus genes (Ttr, Kl, Folr1). Six regions remained, with 17,809 spots. The classifier was the same leave-one-section-out penalised logistic regression. It used four feature sets: QC metrics, signature scores, principal components and highly variable genes. Each set predicted treatment and, separately, slide. Treatment was judged against the 84-relabelling permutation null and by 401's rank among P28052 sections. If any true treatment signal was masked by anatomy, it should now emerge. If slide is the real driver, slide prediction should stay high.
66.results: Removing anatomy changed nothing important. Treatment was still not predictable beyond slide. QC features gave treatment AUC 0.67 (p = 0.30). AUC is the chance that a random BRICHOS section scores above a random PBS section; 0.5 is guessing. Signature scores gave 0.72 (p = 0.16). Principal components gave 0.83 (p = 0.060), the closest any model came. Highly variable genes gave 0.67 (p = 0.095). Slide stayed predictable, with AUC from 0.81 to 1.00. BRICHOS 401 ranked second on its slide for PCA and genes, sixth for QC and fourth for signatures. Treatment and slide models still used the same genes, correlated at r = 0.62. PBS-ward genes included Slc17a7, Cd74, Igkc, Apoe and Cst3, several of them plaque-induced or immune-like. BRICHOS-ward genes included Syt1, S100a9 and Prkar1b. The immune genes fit a "BRICHOS calms" story, but they cannot be separated from slide. **Depth, immediate-early genes, region mix and anatomy are all removable nuisances; slide is not removable in this design.** Only nine sections were available.

67.how: Slide and sequencing depth mostly shift a whole section at once. A contrast between two groups of spots in the same section should therefore cancel them. This run uses that idea. Counts were downsampled to 5,000 UMI per spot, and seven regions shared by all sections were kept (21,874 spots). Microglial signatures were scored: homeostatic, DAM (disease-associated microglia), PIG (plaque-induced genes), MGnD, neuroinflammation, complement and reactive astrocytes. Negative-control signatures were neuronal, synapse, mature oligodendrocyte and endothelial. These should not respond to treatment. Within each section and region, spots were ranked by deconvolution microglia fraction. Deconvolution estimates cell-type shares from a single-cell reference. The "niche contrast" is the mean score of the top 20 % (hot) minus the bottom 50 % (cold). A slope of score on rank was also computed. Section values averaged over regions. PBS (6) and BRICHOS (3) were compared with a Mann–Whitney rank test and a mixed model with a per-section random offset. BRICHOS 401 was ranked among P28052 sections. P24215 BRICHOS minus wild type gave a same-slide reference.
67.results: The plaque-niche response was clear in the Alzheimer model. Hot-minus-cold contrasts were much larger than in wild type. DAM was 0.17 vs 0.02 and PIG 0.22 vs 0.08. MGnD was 0.14 vs 0.02, and complement 0.29 vs 0.16. **The response was fully present under BRICHOS.** On wild type's own slide, BRICHOS minus wild type was +0.14 for DAM and +0.15 for PIG. No microglial niche contrast differed by treatment. The DAM:homeostatic ratio gave p = 0.55 (rank test) and 0.36 (mixed model). Homeostatic gave 0.26 and 0.26; PIG gave 0.38 and 0.45. BRICHOS 401 had the highest DAM, PIG and MGnD contrast on its slide, the opposite of calming. The homeostatic slope was weakly higher under BRICHOS (+0.035, p = 0.095 and 0.068), matching §58's direction. One negative control failed. BRICHOS hot spots were less oligodendrocyte-depleted (+0.075, p = 0.024, mixed model p = 0.003). This was largest in meninges, hypothalamus and caudoputamen. It is unexplained: either slide leaking into the contrast, or a biological lead. Overall, cancelling slide removes the "BRICHOS calms microglia" niche effect.

68.how: Earlier regional rescue tests compared two axes. The disease axis is PBS minus wild type; the rescue axis is BRICHOS minus PBS. Both contain the slide effect with opposite signs, so slide alone can look like rescue. This run uses a difference-in-differences design to cancel region-uniform slide effects. Input is pseudobulk per section and region: summed counts for ten sections and seven shared regions, 14,927 genes, as log2 counts per million. Each section was centred on its own mean across the seven regions. Any shift that is the same in all regions of a section cancels, whether slide, depth or a global treatment effect. Only the regional profile remains. Two disease gene sets were used: 52 PIG genes (plaque-induced) and 219 genes from the earlier PBS-versus-wild-type test. Per region, concordance is the share of disease genes moved toward healthy. Rescue slope regresses rescue change on disease change. Significance used all 84 BRICHOS relabellings. A within-slide design compared 401 with P28052 PBS. Finally, slide variance was split into region-uniform and region-specific parts and compared with same-slide noise.
68.results: Centring kept the regional ranking. With PIG genes, concordance was high in olfactory areas (0.85), infragranular cortex (0.83), meninges and supragranular cortex (0.79). It was low in corpus callosum (0.06) and hypothalamus (0.10). **No region reached significance.** The best permutation p was about 0.13 (infragranular PIG concordance, p = 0.131). The lowest slope p values were 0.167 and 0.214. BRICHOS 401 alone, compared within its own slide, showed the opposite profile. Corpus callosum (0.85) and caudoputamen (0.83) looked most rescued, and supragranular least (0.50). The slide effect was only roughly uniform across regions. Its region-uniform variance was 0.029, about 1.7 times same-slide noise (0.017). Its region-specific variance was 0.070, about 1.3 times noise (0.054). It exceeded 88 % of same-slide noise splits. Each region's slide effect correlated with the average at only 0.54 to 0.62. So the centring assumption of no slide × region interaction holds only approximately. Centring also removes any global rescue by design. The 401-only analysis rests on one section.

69.how: Centring (§68) removes slide but also removes any global rescue. This run tries model-based slide removal instead, keeping treatment. Input is the same section × region pseudobulk. Four methods were tried, each with a different assumption. The "tech" method predicts the slide difference from gene features like GC content, length and expression level, then subtracts it. This assumes slide is a technical bias. RUVs estimates unwanted variation from residuals among samples of the same treatment and region. RUVg removes unwanted variation estimated from control genes that should not respond to treatment. Its 1,000 control genes were expressed, stable across regions and PBS sections, and excluded PIG and disease genes. RUV methods used one or two factors (k). Factors were regressed out together with the treatment × region design. The rescue tests were rerun, with the disease axis recomputed on corrected data. Significance used 84 BRICHOS relabellings, refitting RUV factors each time. Diagnostics measured leftover slide variance against same-slide noise and correlated each factor with slide and treatment.
69.results: The slide effect is not technical. The tech model explained almost none of it (R² 0.013, below same-slide noise at 0.029). RUVg captured slide best: its factor correlated 0.97 with slide. It cut region-uniform slide variance to 0.42 times noise (k = 1) and 0.30 (k = 2). No method reduced the region-specific part, which stayed at 1.13 to 1.27 times noise. After RUVg with k = 1, PIG rescue slopes reached p = 0.024 in infragranular and supragranular cortex. Without correction both were 0.060. With the data-derived gene set, p was 0.012 (infragranular), 0.012 (supragranular), 0.036 (meninges) and 0.048 (olfactory). **The data-set infragranular slope had p = 0.012, the permutation floor, under every method.** With two factors, the PIG cortex p values rose to 0.12 to 0.18. Corpus callosum and hypothalamus never responded. Caveats are important. RUVg assumes BRICHOS leaves the control genes alone. Results depend on k. The cortex rescue rests on the two P24215 BRICHOS sections, and 401 does not reproduce it. The data gene set was chosen on a slide-contaminated contrast.

70.how: This run directly tests whether the rescue-slope statistic is contaminated by slide. The rescue slope regresses each gene's BRICHOS-versus-PBS change on its disease change (PBS versus wild type). A negative slope means genes raised by disease are lowered by BRICHOS. Input was whole-section pseudobulk, meaning all spots in a section summed, as log2 counts per million. Only the 52 PIG genes (plaque-induced genes) were used. Three contrasts were regressed on the same disease change. The slide-only contrast compares the two P24215 BRICHOS sections with BRICHOS 401 on P28052. Both arms are BRICHOS, so it isolates slide. The treatment-only contrast compares 401 with the six PBS sections on the same slide. It isolates treatment but rests on one section. The original contrast is all BRICHOS minus all PBS, mixing treatment and slide. As a reference, each of the seven P28052 sections was compared in turn with the other six. This shows how unusual 401 is on its own slide. The computation runs live in notebook 16 and is repeated in notebook 17.
70.results: **The slide-only contrast gave the steepest "rescue" slope**: −0.098. The treatment-only contrast gave +0.026, pointing the wrong way for rescue. The original contrast gave −0.040, between the two. So the negative slope seen in the original analysis is driven by slide, not treatment. The fraction of PIG genes that went down told a different story. It was 0.37 for slide only, 0.67 for treatment only and 0.60 for the original. Slide pushes PIG genes up, so this concordance measure is not driven by slide. But there was no within-slide evidence of a global PIG rescue. BRICHOS 401 ranked second of seven on its slide for fraction of PIG genes down. PBS section P28052_202 ranked higher, at 0.71. So 401 is not unusual among PBS sections. The conclusion is that the original rescue-slope statistic cannot be read as a treatment effect without slide correction. The treatment-only contrast rests on one section. The slide-only contrast also includes normal animal-to-animal variation.

71.how: This is an overview notebook, not a new analysis. It collects every result that touches the treatment × slide confound, for manuscript framing. It loads saved outputs from earlier notebooks and runs one small live computation, the slide-contrast demo of §70. It brings together a design table with spot counts per section. It adds the region-matched microglia abundance table from §51. It includes the slide-adjusted microglial state model from §62. It shows the within-section niche contrasts from §67, which cancel section-wide shifts. It summarises the treatment classifiers from §63, §64 and §66, which test whether treatment is recognisable in unseen sections. It shows the rescue permutation p values across the slide-removal methods of §68 and §69. Those include RUVg, which removes unwanted variation estimated from control genes that should not respond to treatment. Each control asks the same question in a different way. Does the BRICHOS effect survive when slide is held fixed, modelled or cancelled? A claim that survives several independent checks is more credible than one that survives none. The notebook ends with a draft caveat paragraph.
71.results: The status table sorts claims by how they fared. **The Alzheimer disease response is robust.** PIG and DAM genes rise versus wild type, within sections and on the wild type's own slide. The claim that BRICHOS lowers microglia abundance is gone. The −5.0 % difference (p = 0.38 whole-section, 0.071 region-adjusted) becomes +1.2 % with slide (p = 0.70). The homeostatic state shift is weakened, from p = 0.013 to 0.30 with slide. Calming of plaque-niche microglia is not supported. The classifier learns slide and depth, not treatment. Regional rescue partly survives. Infragranular cortex reaches p = 0.012 to 0.024 after RUVg with one factor, but rests on the two P24215 BRICHOS sections. The original rescue-slope statistics are not usable as they stand. The defensible core is a clear disease response that BRICHOS does not abolish, a modest cortical rescue, and no abundance change. Suggested next steps are placing PBS on the same slide as BRICHOS, or using shared processing batches. Slide-independent validation, such as IBA1, CD68 and P2RY12 staining, is also proposed. The classifier panel mislabels the depth-only run's settings.
